ei.title: 전성현 기말 수능유형 PICK 독해 기본 10지문
ei.subject: 수능유형PICK

fullPassage:
In an experiment, researchers divided people into two groups. The first group was asked, "Is the population of Turkey greater than 35 million? What's your best estimate?" While the answers varied, they were mostly close to 35 million. They then asked the same question to the second group, only with the number changed to 100 million. Although these were both random figures, the second group's estimates were much higher than those of the first group. This shows that people often set their standard of judgment based on the first thoughts they form. In other words, where you start can influence your conclusion. This tendency is intentionally used by some salespeople. They will show you their highest-priced items first in order to raise your estimate of a fair price. To avoid this trap, don't make hasty decisions based on a single starting point or the standards set by others. Instead, learn more about the subject and make an informed decision.

When we try to come up with ideas in groups, we usually use the brainstorming technique. You're probably familiar with how this works. People speak their ideas out loud, and others make comments and share their own thoughts in response. Unfortunately, studies show that there are some significant problems with this commonly used method. The biggest one is called "blocking," which refers to the fact that, in a group setting, only one person can speak at a time. This puts a limit on the number of ideas that are created. While everyone sits and waits for one person to explain his or her idea, they are judging, changing, and even forgetting their own. Moreover, no one gets the chance to say everything they're thinking during a brainstorming session. They have to give everyone else an opportunity to speak as well, so they might lose the chance to share a great idea. What's the solution? Instead of brainstorming, consider "brainwriting." The method is similar, but participants write down their ideas instead of speaking them. Since everyone is producing ideas at the same time, this can solve the problem of blocking. Thus, the total number of ideas at the end will be much greater. Also, no ideas are forgotten or changed while people wait for their turn to speak.

Although taking part in sports can be a positive experience for some children, others are traumatized by the pressure to succeed and humiliation of failing to win. This kind of intense focus on defeating the competition drives kids away from athletics, depriving them of the physical benefits sports can bring. The main problem is that student athletes are constantly being encouraged to outperform their rivals. If they don't, they may suffer a loss of confidence. And even if they do, the pressure to keep winning can be stressful and damaging. We need to blow the whistle on this behavior. Instead of trying to be the best, young athletes should focus on their personal performance. Comparing today's results to yesterday's is a healthy kind of comparison that can lead to personal development. When it comes to school sports, it's time we moved the goalposts inward.

Research has shown that six-month-old babies are able to distinguish not only the faces of other humans but also those of different animal species. However, at around the age of nine months, this skill becomes more specialized - babies get far better at recognizing human faces but lose their ability to tell animal faces apart. In an experiment, researchers tried to discover whether this skill would be retained if the babies saw animal faces on a regular basis. They showed six-month-old babies pictures of some monkey faces and then divided the babies into two groups. The first group was then shown different pictures of monkeys for one or two minutes each day, while the other group was not shown any. After they reached the age of nine months, the researchers tested the babies by showing them a pair of monkey faces, one that they had all seen before in the first stage of the experiment and one that they hadn't. By measuring the amount of time the babies spent looking at the faces, the researchers were able to determine that the first group could recognize the familiar face, while the second could not. This suggests that our tendency to focus only on human faces as we mature arises from the simple fact that we are constantly exposed to them.

Imagine taking a test and being surprised to find that you received an unsatisfactory grade. Most likely, your brain would immediately begin to seek out explanations for this unexpected outcome - perhaps the test was overly difficult or the teacher graded it unfairly. Now imagine you got an A+ on the same test. Instead of searching for an external cause, you would likely attribute the grade to your hard work and intelligence. In psychology, this is known as a self-serving bias. What determines whether we attribute the cause of an outcome to internal or external forces is whether the outcome itself is positive or negative. It is believed that this bias exists as a means of maintaining our self-esteem, allowing us to take credit for the good and avoid accepting blame for the bad. While this is useful, it is also important to learn how to take responsibility for our shortcomings.

People like to have options. In fact, it is a common belief in modern society that the more choices we have, the better our lives will be. This, however, is not necessarily true. Choices can actually have an adverse effect on our happiness. We may begin to worry about all the options we didn't select, wondering if we have made a mistake. What's more, being completely responsible for our own decisions means that we have no one else to blame when things go wrong. This is why people often hesitate to make decisions on their own. Instead, they'll seek out the suggestions and opinions of others. Movie reviews are popular for this reason: people who use them to select which movies to see can always blame the reviewer if the film turns out to be a poor choice.

Do you have photos or videos of interesting animals that you've observed? If so, they may be of use to scientists. In the past, the information contained in such images went largely unused. Now, however, imageomics, a new scientific field that utilizes artificial intelligence, is extracting valuable data from them. Currently, the exact status of many threatened species is unclear due to a lack of information. By tapping into the digital collections of public institutions and private citizens, scientists hope to expand their knowledge and better understand the current range and population of the planet's many animal species. If you haven't posted your animal photos and videos to an imageomics-related website, you should consider doing so. It doesn't take long, and it could make a difference for a rare species facing extinction.

In the past, it was believed that children growing up in multilingual households were at a disadvantage. Experts worried that these children were likely to become confused and never fully master either language. While linguists admit that confusion can be caused by having multiple languages in the home, they now believe there are far more advantages. For one thing, children growing up in this sort of environment must constantly switch between languages. This kind of mental exercise is very useful because it keeps their brain in shape, improves their ability to focus under difficult conditions, and teaches them how to smoothly move from one task to another. These are important skills that give multilingual children an advantage over their classmates.

Has this happened to you? You have a list of tasks to do around the house. You complete the first one and leave the room to move on to the next one. Suddenly, you can't remember what it is! Believe it or not, the act of moving from one room to another may be to blame. This is the theory of researchers who are studying how the brain works. According to them, there are many divided "rooms" in our brain in which we store short-term memories. And when we exit a room in the real world, our mind moves on to a new space as well. So, when you leave the room to accomplish your next task, you're also "leaving behind" the short-term memory that contains your to-do list!

One of the defining characteristics of modern technology is that it progresses at impressive speeds. However, this means that more and more consumers are trading in their used electronic devices for newer models. This has led to a new kind of industry that is being referred to as reCommerce, or reverse commerce. It consists of various services, both online and offline, designed to recover the unwanted products. For example, when the release of the latest version of a popular tablet PC was announced, a reCommerce website purchased 2,000 previously owned models in just one hour. It gave consumers cash or gift cards in return for these devices and then sold them to electronics stores. The stores use these "recycled" electronic devices to attract consumers on a low budget who couldn't afford to buy the new version. In this way, reCommerce benefits both retailers and consumers, and it also helps the planet by reducing the amount of electronic waste and increasing sustainability.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) hasty=성급한, (B) adverse=부정적인/불리한, (C) recover=회수하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① deliberate(신중한) — 함정에 빠지지 않으려면 '성급한' 결정을 피하라는 문맥이므로 deliberate는 반대
✅ ② hasty(성급한) — adverse(부정적인) — recover(회수하다) — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ beneficial(이로운) — 선택지가 행복에 '부정적인(adverse)' 영향을 줄 수 있다는 문맥과 모순
❌ ④ discard(버리다) — 리커머스는 원치 않는 제품을 '회수(recover)'하는 서비스이므로 반대
det.tip: hasty decisions=성급한 결정 / adverse effect=역효과 / recover=회수하다

② intentionally(의도적으로) ✅ 적절 — 판매원들이 기준점 효과를 의도적으로 이용함

det.analysis:
✅ ① mistake(실수) — 선택하지 않은 모든 옵션에 대해 걱정하기 시작하며, 우리가 '실수'를 한 것은 아닌지 궁금해한다는 문맥 ←정답
❌ ② profit(이익) — 이익을 '만들었는지' 걱정하는 문맥이 아님
❌ ③ promise(약속) — 약속과 무관한 문맥
❌ ④ comparison(비교) — make a comparison은 가능하나, 잘못된 선택을 걱정하는 문맥과 맞지 않음

questions.passage: Although taking part in sports can be a positive experience for some children, others are traumatized by the pressure to succeed and humiliation of failing to win. This kind of intense focus on defeating the competition drives kids away from athletics, depriving them of the physical benefits sports can bring. The main problem is that student athletes are constantly being encouraged to outperform their rivals. If they don't, they may suffer a loss of __________. And even if they do, the pressure to keep winning can be stressful and damaging. We need to blow the whistle on this behavior. Instead of trying to be the best, young athletes should focus on their personal performance. Comparing today's results to yesterday's is a healthy kind of comparison that can lead to personal development. When it comes to school sports, it's time we moved the goalposts inward.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경쟁자를 이기지 못하면 '자신감(confidence)' 상실을 겪을 수 있다는 문맥
det.analysis:
❌ ① curiosity(호기심) — 경쟁에서 지는 것과 호기심 상실은 무관
✅ ② confidence(자신감) — 경쟁자를 능가하도록 끊임없이 독려받는 학생 선수들이 그러지 못하면 '자신감' 상실을 겪을 수 있다는 문맥 ←정답
❌ ③ patience(인내심) — 패배로 잃는 것은 인내심이 아님
❌ ④ generosity(관대함) — 문맥과 무관

questions.passage: In the past, it was believed that children growing up in multilingual households were at a __________. Experts worried that these children were likely to become confused and never fully master either language. While linguists admit that confusion can be caused by having multiple languages in the home, they now believe there are far more advantages. For one thing, children growing up in this sort of environment must constantly switch between languages. This kind of mental exercise is very useful because it keeps their brain in shape, improves their ability to focus under difficult conditions, and teaches them how to smoothly move from one task to another. These are important skills that give multilingual children an advantage over their classmates.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과거에는 다중언어 가정에서 자라는 아이들이 '불리하다(at a disadvantage)'고 여겨졌다는 문맥
det.analysis:
❌ ① glance(흘긋 봄) — at a glance=한눈에. 문맥과 무관
❌ ② distance(거리) — at a distance=멀리서. 문맥과 무관
✅ ③ disadvantage(불리함) — 과거에는 다중언어 가정의 아이들이 언어에 혼란을 겪어 '불리한 처지'라고 믿어졌다는 문맥. 뒤에 전문가들의 걱정 내용이 이어짐 ←정답
❌ ④ loss(상실) — at a loss=어쩔 줄 모르는. 아이들 자체가 어쩔 줄 모른다는 뜻이 아니라 불리하다는 평가가 문맥에 맞음

questions.passage: Do you have photos or videos of interesting animals that you've <u>observed</u>? If so, they may be of use to scientists. In the past, the information contained in such images went largely unused. Now, however, imageomics, a new scientific field that utilizes artificial intelligence, is extracting valuable data from them. Currently, the exact status of many threatened species is unclear due to a lack of information. By tapping into the digital collections of public institutions and private citizens, scientists hope to expand their knowledge and better understand the current range and population of the planet's many animal species. If you haven't posted your animal photos and videos to an imageomics-related website, you should consider doing so. It doesn't take long, and it could make a difference for a rare species facing extinction.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 observed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: observed=관찰했다 → watched(지켜보았다)와 가장 가까움
det.analysis:
✅ ① watched(지켜본) — observe=관찰하다. 당신이 '관찰한' 흥미로운 동물들의 사진이라는 문맥 ←정답
❌ ② raised(기른) — 동물을 길렀다는 뜻이 아님
❌ ③ trained(훈련시킨) — 훈련과 무관
❌ ④ drawn(그린) — 사진·영상 속 동물을 '본' 것이지 그린 것이 아님

questions.passage: Has this happened to you? You have a list of tasks to do around the house. You complete the first one and leave the room to move on to the next one. Suddenly, you can't remember what it is! Believe it or not, the act of moving from one room to another may be to blame. This is the theory of researchers who are studying how the brain works. According to them, there are many divided "rooms" in our brain in which we store short-term memories. And when we exit a room in the real world, our mind moves on to a new space as well. So, when you leave the room to <u>accomplish</u> your next task, you're also "leaving behind" the short-term memory that contains your to-do list!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 accomplish와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: accomplish=완수하다 → complete(끝마치다)와 가장 가까움
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandon(포기하다) — 반대 방향의 의미
✅ ② complete(끝마치다) — accomplish=완수하다. 다음 할 일을 '완수하러' 방을 나선다는 문맥 ←정답
❌ ③ postpone(미루다) — 할 일을 미루는 것이 아니라 하러 가는 문맥
❌ ④ assign(배정하다) — 과제를 배정하는 것과 무관

questions.passage: Research has shown that six-month-old babies are able to distinguish not only the faces of other humans but also those of different animal species. However, at around the age of nine months, this skill becomes more specialized - babies get far better at recognizing human faces but lose their ability to tell animal faces apart. In an experiment, researchers tried to discover whether this skill would be retained if the babies saw animal faces on a regular basis. They showed six-month-old babies pictures of some monkey faces and then divided the babies into two groups. The first group was then shown different pictures of monkeys for one or two minutes each day, while the other group was not shown any. After they reached the age of nine months, the researchers tested the babies by showing them a pair of monkey faces, one that they had all seen before in the first stage of the experiment and one that they hadn't. By measuring the amount of time the babies spent looking at the faces, the researchers were able to <u>determine</u> that the first group could recognize the familiar face, while the second could not. This suggests that our tendency to focus only on human faces as we mature arises from the simple fact that we are constantly exposed to them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 determine과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: determine=알아내다/판단하다 → conclude(결론 내리다)와 가장 가까움
det.analysis:
❌ ① deny(부인하다) — 연구 결과를 부인한 것이 아님
❌ ② predict(예측하다) — 실험 '후' 알아낸 것이므로 예측이 아님
❌ ③ measure(측정하다) — 측정(measuring)은 수단이었고, determine은 그 결과 '알아냈다'는 뜻
✅ ④ conclude(결론 내리다) — 아기들이 얼굴을 보는 시간을 측정함으로써 첫 번째 집단이 익숙한 얼굴을 알아본다고 '판단/결론 내릴' 수 있었다는 문맥 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 expand와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: expand=확장하다 ↔ shrink(줄어들다/축소하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① shrink(축소하다) — expand(확장하다)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② maintain(유지하다) — 늘리지도 줄이지도 않는 중립 의미로 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ share(공유하다) — 확장·축소 축과 무관
❌ ④ borrow(빌리다) — 지식을 빌린다는 다른 축의 의미

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 valuable과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: valuable=가치 있는 ↔ worthless(가치 없는). priceless는 '값을 매길 수 없을 만큼 귀중한'이므로 오히려 동의 방향
det.analysis:
❌ ① priceless(값을 매길 수 없는) — 함정. price+less지만 '너무 귀중해서 값을 매길 수 없다'는 뜻으로 valuable과 같은 방향
✅ ② worthless(가치 없는) — valuable(가치 있는)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ temporary(일시적인) — 시간 축의 의미로 가치 축과 무관
❌ ④ ordinary(평범한) — 특별함 축의 의미로 가치의 유무와는 다른 축

questions.passage:
(A) It is believed that this bias exists as a means of maintaining our self-esteem, allowing us to take <u>credit</u> for the good and avoid accepting blame for the bad.

(B) She didn't have enough cash for the new refrigerator, so she bought it on <u>credit</u> and paid a little every month.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 credit의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) take credit for=~에 대한 공로를 차지하다, (B) on credit=외상으로(신용 거래로)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 학점 — (B) 외상: (A)는 좋은 결과의 '공로'를 차지한다는 뜻이지 학점이 아님
❌ ② (A) 공로 — (B) 학점: (B)는 현금이 부족해 '외상(신용 거래)'으로 샀다는 뜻
✅ ③ (A) 공로 — (B) 외상(신용 거래): (A) take credit for the good=좋은 것에 대한 공로를 차지하다, (B) buy on credit=신용 거래로 사다 ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 외상 — (B) 공로: 두 문맥의 의미가 뒤바뀜
det.tip: credit: 공로(take credit for), 외상·신용(on credit), 학점 등 다의어

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a guess or judgment about the size, amount, or value of something"

det.korean: estimate=추정(치). 크기·양·가치에 대한 추측이나 판단
det.analysis:
✅ ① estimate(추정치) — 크기·양·가치에 대한 추측·판단 ←정답
❌ ② standard(기준) — 판단의 잣대가 되는 기준이지 추측이 아님
❌ ③ conclusion(결론) — 생각 끝에 내린 최종 판단으로, 양·가치에 대한 '추측'이 아님
❌ ④ figure(수치) — 숫자 자체를 가리키며 '추측'의 의미가 없음

questions.passage: Currently, the exact status of many threatened species is unclear due to a lack of information. By __________ (tap) into the digital collections of public institutions and private citizens, scientists hope to expand their knowledge and better understand the current range and population of the planet's many animal species.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: tap → tapping. 전치사 By 뒤에는 동명사
det.analysis: By + 동명사: '~함으로써'. 전치사 by의 목적어 자리에 동사가 오면 동명사(-ing) 형태가 되어야 함. tap into(활용하다) → tapping
det.tip: By tapping into=~을 활용함으로써. 전치사 뒤 동사는 동명사

questions.passage: What's more, __________ (be) completely responsible for our own decisions means that we have no one else to blame when things go wrong. This is why people often hesitate to make decisions on their own.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: be → being. 동사 means의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구
det.analysis: 동명사 주어: '__________ completely responsible ~ decisions'가 동사 means의 주어이므로 동사원형 be가 아니라 동명사 being이 필요. being responsible=책임지는 것
det.tip: 동명사구 주어: Being responsible ... means ~ = 책임지는 것은 ~을 의미한다

Comparing today's results to yesterday's is a healthy kind of comparison that can lead to personal development. When it comes to school sports, it's time we moved the goalposts inward.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이런 행태에 '제동을 걸어야(호루라기를 불어야)' 한다는 문맥. blow the whistle on=~을 중단시키다/고발하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① break the ice(어색한 분위기를 깨다) — 승리 압박을 비판하는 문맥과 무관
❌ ② beat around the bush(빙빙 돌려 말하다) — 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ pull some strings(연줄을 동원하다) — 문맥과 무관
✅ ④ blow the whistle(호루라기를 불다, 제동을 걸다) — 승리에만 집착하는 행태를 '중단시켜야 한다'는 문맥. 스포츠 소재와 어울리는 비유 ←정답
det.tip: blow the whistle on=~에 제동을 걸다, ~을 고발하다

questions.passage: In an experiment, researchers divided people into two groups. The first group was asked, "Is the population of Turkey greater than 35 million? What's your best estimate?" While the answers varied, they were mostly close to 35 million. They then asked the same question to the second group, only with the number changed to 100 million. Although these were both random figures, the second group's estimates were much higher than those of the first group. This shows that people often set their __________ based on the first thoughts they form. In other words, where you start can influence your conclusion. This tendency is intentionally used by some salespeople. They will show you their highest-priced items first in order to raise your estimate of a fair price. To avoid this trap, don't make hasty decisions based on a single starting point or the standards set by others. Instead, learn more about the subject and make an informed decision.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 처음 형성한 생각에 근거해 '판단의 기준(standard of judgment)'을 설정한다는 문맥 (기준점 효과)
det.analysis:
❌ ① margin of error(오차 범위) — 통계 용어로, 첫 생각을 기준 삼는다는 문맥과 무관
✅ ② standard of judgment(판단의 기준) — 터키 인구 실험에서 처음 제시된 숫자(35 million/100 million)가 추정치를 좌우했듯, 사람들은 처음 형성한 생각으로 '판단의 기준'을 세운다는 결론 ←정답
❌ ③ point of view(관점) — 관점이 아니라 판단의 '기준점'이 핵심
❌ ④ course of action(행동 방침) — 행동 계획이 아니라 판단 기준에 관한 문맥
det.tip: set a standard of judgment=판단 기준을 세우다 (앵커링 효과)
